01 / 06 · AI agents

Agent Invest

Multi-agent investment monitoring · built with a teammate

Full-stack system: FastAPI backend and Next.js dashboard where several AI agents analyse symbols, store predictions and compare them with later prices to track accuracy per timeframe. Builds daily reports and talks to users through a Telegram bot by command or natural language.

Walkthrough
ProblemFollowing many symbols by hand is slow, and nobody knows whether an AI's calls were any good.
How it works
  1. Several AI agents analyse each symbol
  2. Predictions are stored with their timeframe
  3. Later prices are compared with the stored predictions
  4. Accuracy is tracked per timeframe on the Next.js dashboard
  5. A daily report is built; users ask the Telegram bot by command or natural language
ControlsPredictions are judged against real later prices instead of trusting the model's own confidence.
When showing itTeam project: open the dashboard, then the repo linked on the card.

02 / 06 · Automation

LendLoop

Loan tracking with automated, idempotent reminders

Web app for tracking money lent to friends. Next.js and TypeScript with Clerk auth and a Convex backend; n8n sends reminders through HMAC-signed webhooks with retries and backoff, and each reminder is idempotent so nobody is nagged twice. Built as a take-home project.

Walkthrough
ProblemLending money to friends means remembering who owes what, and nagging without annoying anyone.
How it works
  1. User signs in (Clerk) and records a loan
  2. Convex stores the loan and due date
  3. n8n finds loans that need a reminder
  4. n8n calls the app through an HMAC-signed webhook
  5. The reminder goes out once; failures retry with backoff (up to 5 times)
ControlsSigned requests, timestamps older than 5 minutes rejected, idempotent handlers so a retry never sends a second reminder.
When showing itBuilt as a take-home project: show the webhook handler and the retry log in the repo.

Source on GitHub →

LINE AI Assistant for a Repair Shop

Diagnosis help for staff, service reminders for customers

One LINE Official Account serving two audiences: staff send fault codes or symptoms for an AI diagnosis and log completed jobs; customers link their LINE to their phone number and receive a reminder when the ~6-month service is due. A daily scheduler inside the same process pushes the reminders.

Walkthrough
ProblemStaff lose time diagnosing faults, and customers forget their 6-month service.
How it works
  1. Staff message the LINE account with a fault code or symptom
  2. An LLM drafts a diagnosis for staff to use

  4. Customers link their LINE to their phone number

ControlsThe AI only advises staff; customers get scheduled reminders, not free-form AI answers. Several API keys are rotated to survive rate limits.

04 / 06 · Security

AppSec Testing & Remediation (OWASP Juice Shop)

Found and documented 3 real vulnerabilities (SQL injection auth bypass, IDOR, SQL injection + info disclosure) in a locally-run copy of OWASP's own intentionally-vulnerable training app, then patched the vulnerable code and re-verified against the original requests that the fixes held while legitimate use kept working. Full requests/responses and the code diff are in the reports.

Walkthrough
ProblemShow I can find, fix and re-verify web vulnerabilities, not only list them.
How it works
  1. Run OWASP Juice Shop v20.2.0 locally
  2. Find and document 3 vulnerabilities with full requests and responses
  3. Patch the vulnerable code
  4. Replay the original exploit requests against the fix
  5. Confirm normal login, own basket and search still work
ControlsFixes use parameterised queries and a server-side ownership check from the session token; exploits now fail safely with 401/403 or an empty result and no stack trace.
When showing itOpen the two PDFs: Findings first, then Remediation with the code diff. Training app only, no real client.

002

AI security

Agents that call tools need controls the model cannot talk its way around. This is how I design them, and what I have tested hands-on.

Threat model for a tool-calling agent

  • Prompt injectionContain the blast radius: read-only tools by default, untrusted text kept apart from instructions.
  • Excessive agencyHuman approval for anything that writes, sends or spends; a kill switch; risky actions off by default.
  • Forged webhooksHMAC-signed requests both ways, timestamps older than 5 minutes rejected (built into LendLoop).
  • Duplicate side effectsIdempotent handlers and retries with backoff, every attempt logged (LendLoop: 5 retries).
  • Leaked keys and cost abuseKeys stay server-side, rotated across several keys (LINE repair bot), rate and token limits.
  • Cross-user data accessAuthorization checked on the server from the session, never from request parameters (Juice Shop fix).
# illustrative trace: a guarded agent step
agent  > tool_call  send_email(to="customer", body=...)
policy > tenant=A  scope=read_only  BLOCKED: write action
policy > route to human approval
human  > approved  (logged: user, time, inputs)
agent  > executed once  (idempotency key checked)

Hands-on: OWASP Juice Shop

A deliberately vulnerable training app on my own machine, assessed like a client engagement, then fixed and re-tested.

SeverityFindingFix
CriticalSQL injection login bypassParameterised query
HighIDOR on basket APIOwnership check from session token
MediumSQL injection in search + verbose errorsParameterised query, safe error response

Exploit requests fail safely after the patch (401/403 or empty result, no stack trace) and normal login, own basket and search still work. Training app only, no real client.

SAR Crop-Damage Verification

Parcel-level flood & crop damage from free satellite radar

Turns open Sentinel-1 SAR imagery into per-plot flood and crop-damage estimates for Thai rice insurers and lenders.   4. Attach scene IDs, versions, parameters and a confidence score

003

Approach

Three habits that show up across the projects above.

01

Verify before claiming

Numbers get checked against an independent calculation before they ship. Every fee table here cites its source and date.

02

Humans stay in the loop

Publishing, payments and anything irreversible wait for an explicit approval step. Automation drafts; people decide.

03

Ship small, measure

Start with the smallest version a real user can try, put it online, and let usage decide what gets built next.

004

How a build ships

Four stages I follow on every project. Click a stage; this is an illustrative walk-through of my process, not a live system.

Pin down the pain

Write down what is slow, manual or unreliable, who approves what, and what 'done' means. Agree the smallest version worth trying.

Scope noteApproval pointsSuccess check

Draw the flow and the guardrails

Choose the pieces (n8n, FastAPI, a bot), decide where a human must approve, and define how every number will be verified.

Flow diagramData checksFailure handling

Small steps, tested as I go

Ship a thin working slice first. Retries, idempotency and logging go in early, then features. Tests compare results with an independent calculation.

Thin sliceTestsLogs

Online, documented, handed over

Deploy with Docker or Cloudflare Pages, write the README and a short runbook, and watch real usage before adding more.

DeployedDocsFollow-up
